subject.title: [security] GCP cleanup can delete labeled instances without an exact local claim

question: Should direct GCP cleanup and release adopt the same exact local-claim fail-closed contract as AWS and the VISION ownership boundary before deleting GCE instances?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the repair changes the destructive-operation boundary for operators who currently rely on label-only direct GCP cleanup or release after local state loss.

options.title: Adopt fail-closed claim guard
options.body: Require an exact project/resource/slug/zone-bound GCP claim before destructive delete, and document explicit reclaim/adoption for lost local state.

options.title: Keep label-only GCP cleanup
options.body: Preserve current best-effort direct cleanup behavior, but accept that mutable GCP labels remain destructive authority despite the security boundary concern.

options.title: Scope cleanup before release
options.body: Guard bulk cleanup first while leaving ReleaseLease for a separate compatibility decision, reducing one path but leaving part of the report open.

recommendation.title: Adopt fail-closed claim guard
recommendation.body: Require an exact project/resource/slug/zone-bound GCP claim before destructive delete, and document explicit reclaim/adoption for lost local state.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work by steipete owns the closest cloud cleanup and exact-claim hardening context.
